Knowing we can never finish that series with her understanding what's going on breaks my heart. Burnsville Center is less than fifteen minutes away from the Mall of America, which is likely why there are so few shoppers. But it was the closest mall to my friend’s apartment and we loved it there.

author: @semisemicoloncolon
text: I really appreciate how Ryan doesn’t just blindly praise and hype up products such as this one, like a lot of other YouTubers would. He’s instead really transparent in his coverage of them and doesn’t shy away from the ways it falls short. It has a really optimistic message, to me, about the importance of humanity and detaching from this technology that, though fancy, won’t replace the authentic human experience, and it’s incredibly refreshing amidst the storm of hyper-tech focused media with depressing implications that we find ourselves in. It’s this kind of genuineness that keeps me coming back to Ryan’s content, though I’m probably older than most of his audience. He is more concerned with doing good than retaining viewership and making money, and I wish I could say the same about more content creators, especially those geared towards younger audiences. He kinda feels like a modern Mr. Rogers in that sense; just a genuine kind soul.

text: 11:03 Hello Ryan! The reason the Golden Gate Bridge has the word “golden” in its name is not because the bridge is gold-colored, but because it spans the Golden Gate Strait, the narrow waterway connecting the Pacific Ocean to San Francisco Bay. The strait was named “Golden Gate” in 1846 by explorer John C. Frémont, who believed it would become a valuable gateway for trade and opportunity, much like a “golden gate” to the Pacific. When the bridge was built decades later, it simply took the name of the strait it crossed. In fact, the bridge is painted a distinctive reddish-orange color called International Orange, which was chosen because it stands out well against the region’s frequent fog. So, even though the bridge is not actually golden, its name comes from the historic waterway beneath it rather than its appearance.

author: @beniamincondrea5292
text: I just wanted to to share some of what I went through. I went to University of San Diego D1 running program. I lived in Oregon and wanted to experience life outside my comfort zone so I looked for colleges outside of my state. If you want to experience life outside of your comfort zone, try to contact coaches outside of your state during your Junior year of high school, because chances are the coaches won't see you. You can make phone calls with the coach and ask him specific questions like, "What times should I try to hit in the 3k, 8k, 1500m", "Is the school more focused more on distance running?", etc. Even better, visit the campus and participate in a training session to get a feel of how their training is like. Most coaches look for work ethic, and the difference in training will be significant from high school to college. Here's a perspective of how training was in college: 6:00AM - 9:00AM Morning speed work, 11:45AM - 12:30PM Weights/Dynamic Stretching, 5:00PM - 6:30PM OYO (on your own, usually 6-8 mile run).
